title: Critical Connections in a Network
statement: There are `n` servers labeled 0..n-1 and undirected connections. A critical connection is a bridge: an edge whose removal increases the number of connected components. Return every bridge as [u, v] with u less than v, sorted lexicographically.
hints: A DFS discovery time and a low-link value are enough. low[v] is the smallest discovery time reachable from v without using the parent edge.
The edge u-v, with u the parent, is a bridge when low[v] is strictly greater than disc[u]. The child cannot reach the parent or anything above it.
Ignore the edge back to the parent, but do use other back edges to lower the low-link value.

approaches.name: Remove each edge and recheck connectivity
approaches.explanation: Fine for tiny graphs and a useful oracle.

editorial: Assign increasing discovery times as DFS enters each node. A child's low-link is the minimum of its own discovery time, the low-links of its children, and the discovery times of back edges. If after exploring a child its low-link stays above the parent's discovery time, the tree edge is the only connection and it is a bridge.

examples.explanation: The edge from 1 to 3 is the only bridge.
